auditMethod.inventory: All tracked Markdown files were inventoried by path, headings, size and SHA-256. Roles, index coverage and local Markdown links/anchors were checked; current product/design/index/competitor documents and relevant contracts were semantically reviewed. This is not a claim that every historical result was rerun.
auditMethod.localLinkParser: Inline Markdown links outside fenced code, file targets and GitHub-style heading anchors; baseline unchanged malformed or generated cases would require manual review.
auditMethod.networkScope: Official release APIs, stable manifest, official documentation source and browser-observed public pages; no installs, uploads, logins, software execution or policy-law re-audit.

findings.action: Refresh four products and make spec the sole current product-status matrix

findings.problem: Spec mixed detailed implementation history, accepted work, blocked prerequisites and new ideas
findings.action: Condense status table and separate acceptance, accepted direction, prerequisites and research candidates

findings.problem: DESIGN front matter contained obsolete palette/component values not present in current token source
findings.action: Remove obsolete scaffold palette/component metadata; retain valid rem-radius contract and current CSS-token source.

findings.problem: Source release catalog contract missing from contract index; one lyric verification report lacked incoming links
Release-note files and old release narrative could be mistaken for published/upgraded state
findings.action: Separate published release, working tree and installed-upgrade receipt; preserve historical release notes

findings.problem: Research index mixed product sources and a version-specific website draft with ongoing engineering entries
findings.action: Create a product/research section and label the v0.4.0 draft as historical

findings.problem: Historical snapshots can be mistaken for current development commitments
findings.action: Keep original dated reports, ADR decisions and release notes; document classification by purpose rather than mass-moving files
